study: Coyne et al. 2013 (Early Reading Intervention [ERI] supplemental K reading; replication study)
eval_evidence: Study run and authored by the Project ERI research team under IES Grant R324E060067 (Texas A&M); the same research team designed the PD and delivered it ('Project ERI researcher team members led both professional development sessions... the same researchers also provided PD during the initial study').
developer_evidence: 'Project ERI researcher team members led both professional development sessions' for the ERI interventionists; the research team delivered the PD directly.
cascade_evidence: ERI research-team members delivered the PD directly to the classroom teachers/interventionists; no train-the-trainer intermediary.
counterfactual_evidence: Comparison is an ACTIVE alternative: a 'school-designed intervention' (SDI), a typical-practice supplemental reading intervention also taught 30 min/day in small groups for ~equivalent sessions; SDI teachers had prior evidence-based-reading PD and FCRR resources (SDI in fact slightly outperformed ERI).
coaching_evidence: Support = two PD sessions plus research staff observing each interventionist three times (fidelity observation with feedback on a 1-4 scale); light/periodic, not recurring in-class coaching cycles.
student_dose_evidence: ERI is a supplemental pull-out small-group beginning-reading intervention delivered to at-risk kindergartners 30 min/day, 5 days/week, ~100 sessions — a direct student-facing dose beyond regular instruction (both arms receive a supplemental dose).
maturity_evidence: Program designed as a single kindergarten year of supplemental small-group intervention (~100 sessions across one school year), measured at end of that year; no multi-year maturity axis.
